analysis.note: Formally also Prathama dual, but here taken as Dvitiya dual object of kṛtvā; Śaṅkara glosses it directly with same/tulye. Revised to the unhyphenated prakriyā stem sukhaduḥkha; the verifier’s dvandva-relation rejection is only reported as unsupported/logged, so the dvandva analysis is retained.

analysis.note: Pausal tataḥ appears as tato before yuddhāya by external sandhi.
Dative of purpose/goal with yujyasva: ‘for/to battle’.
2nd singular imperative in a passive/yak-form; Śaṅkara’s gloss ghaṭāsva gives the idiomatic sense ‘apply yourself, strive’, not merely literal ‘be yoked’.
Fused with evam in the printed naivaṃ.
Underlying evam; in naivaṃ, na + evam gives nai-, and final -m is written anusvāra before pāpam.
Neuter accusative singular substantive object of avāpsyasi: ‘sin/evil’.
Simple future, 2nd singular: ‘you will incur/obtain’; the prefixed lexical form is avāp.

justifications.decision: same is not merely ‘same’ in a loose lexical sense: Śaṅkara glosses it as tulye, and explains the point of this equalizing as not producing rāga and dveṣa toward pleasure and pain.
options_considered: make pleasure and pain physically level
regard pleasure and pain as simply identical
treat pleasure and pain equally, without attachment and aversion
justifications.chosen: “Having made pleasure and pain alike—without forming attachment and aversion.”

evidence.quote: sukha-duḥkhe same tulye kṛtvā, rāga-dveṣāv apy akṛtvety etat |
evidence.translation: Having made pleasure and pain the same, equal; that is, also not having made attachment and aversion.

justifications.decision: The verse has same only with the neuter dual sukha-duḥkhe, but Śaṅkara explicitly supplies samau kṛtvā for the two masculine dual pairs lābhālābhau and jayājayau. The translation therefore repeats ‘alike/equal’ for both pairs.
options_considered: take same as agreeing only with sukha-duḥkhe and leave the other pairs unqualified
make all three contrast-pairs objects of kṛtvā with equalizing supplied for the latter two
justifications.chosen: “and likewise gain and loss, victory and defeat alike.”

evidence.quote: tathā lābhālābhau jayājayau ca samau kṛtvā tato yuddhāya yujyasva ghaṭāsva |
evidence.translation: Likewise, having made gain-and-loss and victory-and-defeat equal, then apply yourself for battle; strive.

justifications.decision: yuddhāya is construed as the dative goal/purpose of yujyasva, and yujyasva is translated idiomatically from Śaṅkara’s ghaṭāsva, ‘strive/apply yourself,’ rather than as a bare literal ‘be yoked’.

evidence.quote: tathā lābhālābhau jayājayau ca samau kṛtvā tato yuddhāya yujyasva ghaṭāsva |
evidence.translation: Likewise, having made gain-and-loss and victory-and-defeat equal, then apply yourself for battle; strive.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara expands evam as modifying the manner of fighting—evaṃ yuddhaṃ kurvan—not as an adjective to pāpam (‘such sin’). pāpam is the accusative object of avāpsyasi.
options_considered: you will not incur such a sin
in this way, while fighting, you will not incur sin
justifications.chosen: “fighting thus, you will not incur sin (pāpa).”

evidence.quote: na evaṃ yuddhaṃ kurvan pāpam avāpsyasi |
evidence.translation: Fighting in this way, you will not incur sin.

justifications.decision: This contextual scope does not change the bare sentence meaning, but it prevents over-reading the verse as Śaṅkara’s main tātparya; he calls this upadeśa prāsaṅgika and says that paramārtha-darśana is the present topic.
options_considered: make this verse the main doctrinal conclusion
read it as an incidental instruction within the broader teaching whose main topic is paramārtha-darśana
justifications.chosen: Treat the verse as an incidental practical instruction in Śaṅkara’s sequence, not the final doctrinal purport.

evidence.quote:
ity eṣa upadeśaḥ prāsaṅgikaḥ ||bhgs_2.38||
paramārtha-darśanam iha prakṛtam |
evidence.translation: Thus this instruction is incidental. The vision of ultimate reality is what is under discussion here.

translation:
Making pleasure and pain alike—without forming attachment and aversion (rāga-dveṣa)—
and likewise gain and loss, victory and defeat alike,
then apply yourself to battle;
fighting thus, you will not incur sin (pāpa).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering might leave lābhālābhau and jayājayau without the supplied ‘equal/alike’; Śaṅkara explicitly supplies samau kṛtvā for them.
It might translate yujyasva literally as ‘be yoked’ or doctrinally as ‘practice yoga,’ missing Śaṅkara’s ghaṭāsva, ‘apply yourself/strive’.
It might take evam with pāpam—‘such sin’—instead of with the manner of fighting; Śaṅkara expands it as evaṃ yuddhaṃ kurvan.
It might miss that equalizing pleasure and pain entails not producing attachment and aversion (rāga-dveṣa).
It might present the verse as the main purport of the teaching, whereas Śaṅkara calls this upadeśa prāsaṅgika and keeps paramārtha-darśana as the main topic.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 represents sukha-duḥkhe, lābhālābhau, and jayājayau as compound-part plus final member; this apparatus records each as a single dvandva compound stem, with members separately in samāsa analysis. For sukha-duḥkhe the prakriyā/checking lemma is now written unhyphenated as sukhaduḥkha, while surface_in_sandhi preserves the printed hyphen.
ByT5’s DuANe tags leave Prathama/Dvitiya ambiguity for sukha-duḥkhe and same; here both are fixed as Dvitiya dual because they are governed by kṛtvā in Śaṅkara’s gloss.
ByT5 labels kṛtvā as a converb; the required schema has no separate converb category, so it is recorded as an avyaya with root kṛ and Kartari sense.
ByT5 lemmatizes avāpsyasi as prefixed avāp; per the requested format it is analyzed as bare root āp with prefix ava.
